title: Workspace session snapshot
description: This JSON representation stores Core-owned, versioned session state outside Note files, Git history, and `schema.sql` derived-index tables. Storage is partitioned by Workspace ID. The persistence layer replaces supported snapshots atomically by writing a temporary file and renaming it. Corrupt bytes, schema-valid but semantically invalid state, and unsupported later `schema_version` values are quarantined and preserved byte-for-byte without migration or overwrite. Runtime uses an empty session for only the active Workspace and never restores malformed state. For malformed current-version state, the default is writable at the normal path after quarantine. A supported current snapshot after a later-version refusal may be written only at an explicitly safe path isolated from the preserved bytes. Core additionally validates active-Workspace equality, identity validity, and active-Note membership because JSON Schema can't express those runtime relationships portably. The snapshot contains no Note body, credential, or device preference. The current schema version is 1.

schema_version.description: Version of this persisted session payload. Version 1 is the current version.

workspace_id.description: Nonempty identity of the Workspace that owns this snapshot. Core requires it to equal the active Workspace identity before restore.

open_note_ids.description: Unique, nonempty Concept IDs of open Notes, in restore order.

active_note_id.description: Nonempty Concept ID of the active Note, or null when no Note is active. Core requires a non-null value to appear in `open_note_ids`.

expanded_directory_ids.description: Unique, nonempty Directory concept IDs or bundle-relative paths used by the Workspace tree.

search_query.description: The most recent search-box text. An empty string is valid.

sync_presentation.description: A presentation-only synchronization label. Version 1 permits only `local`, `connected`, and `paused`. Add values only with a schema-version bump. These values do not define a Git reconciliation state machine.
